media:group.media:title: Public Scholarship: Integral to the Next Generation of Research #concordia #research #mtl #education
media:group.media:description:
The Concordia Public Scholars Program brought an incredible group of researchers together for 2025 - 2026, each bringing a new way of making research more public. Through policy, art, research-creation, electrification, biodiversity, or nostalgia, these scholars created public-facing events that fostered research connections and public dialogue.
Stay tuned for the 2026 - 2027 Public Scholar events!
You can find the previous year's cohort events in the playlist linked in below 🔗

media:group.media:title: 5-Minute Research Talks (5MRT) Postdoctoral Showcase
media:group.media:description:
How much can you learn about cutting-edge research in just five minutes?
Join us for Concordia’s first 5-Minute Research Showcase, where postdoctoral scholars from across disciplines take on the challenge to present their research in an accessible, engaging and compelling way for a broad audience.
Inspired by research communication formats such as the 3-Minute Thesis competition, the showcase challenges researchers to communicate the purpose, significance and impact of their work using visuals and storytelling. Each presenter will have up to five minutes to introduce the questions driving their research and why they matter.
The event celebrates the diverse research being carried out by Concordia’s postdoctoral community while giving researchers an opportunity to strengthen their communication and presentation skills, connect with audiences beyond their fields and spark new interdisciplinary conversations. The 5-Minute Research Talks model is designed specifically for postdoctoral scholars and emphasizes knowledge translation, effective presentation design and audience engagement.
Come discover the breadth of research happening at Concordia and support our postdoctoral scholars as they take on the five-minute challenge.

entry.title: The Iron Ring Podcast: What we wish we knew

media:group.media:title: The Iron Ring Podcast: What we wish we knew
media:group.media:description:
Join us for the new episode recording of The Iron Ring Podcast, where WIE hosts Maria Abou Ghazaly, Zineb Bamouh and Allison Shkodra share their experiences navigating engineering at different stages of their academic journeys.
Through the perspective of women navigating a traditionally male-dominated field, the conversation aims to bridge the gap between newer and more experienced engineering students. From academics and internships to finding balance, building connections, and navigating university life, we’ll reflect on what we’ve learned, the challenges we’ve faced, and what we wish we had known when starting out.

entry.title: Ways of Doing Scenography: Light, Memory, and Research-Creation from Valparíso to Montréal

media:group.media:title: Ways of Doing Scenography: Light, Memory, and Research-Creation from Valparíso to Montréal
media:group.media:description:
This public conversation with Tamara Figueroa explores ways of doing scenography through light, memory, territory, and research-creation. Drawing from her practice as a lighting designer, performance designer, and academic from Valparaíso, Chile, the event will address how live arts can produce knowledge, how professional scenic production can generate methodologies for academic research, and how port cities such as Valparaíso and Montréal can open shared imaginaries around movement, memory, ecologies, and ways of inhabiting.
The conversation introduces her current project, Topologías de los sueños, which is in an initial phase and will be developed through the Centro de Investigaciones Artísticas and the Área de Creación at the Escuela de Teatro, Universidad de Valparaíso.
Tamara Figueroa is an academic visitor from Valparaiso in residency in LePARC from September 23rd to September 29th.

entry.title: A Closer Look: engAGE Centre for Research on Aging

media:group.media:title: A Closer Look: engAGE Centre for Research on Aging
media:group.media:description:
Join us for the next installment of tour Closer Look series - exploring the many labs and spaces across Concordia University, giving you a closer look at what happens here!
This session takes us to the engAGE Centre for Research on Aging with Public Scholar Annick Maugile Flavien and engAGE coordinator Eric Craven to give us a closer look on what is happening in the Centre!
engAGE brings together researchers from a broad range of disciplines, from fine art to physics, to explore creative ways to study age and explore opportunities to enhance health and wellbeing across the life course.
The tour is followed by a discussion with recent awardees of the Grace Dart Foundation Knowledge Mobilization Fund.

media:group.media:title: CTRL + AI: Playing with Intelligence
media:group.media:description:
CTRL + AI: Playing with Intelligence brings together Eldad Tsabary and Scott DeJong for a participatory conversation about what games and simulated worlds can reveal about artificial intelligence and about us.
Tsabary’s Village is a persistent AI world populated by characters who remember, develop relationships, acquire expertise and continue interacting when the user/creator is absent. What began as an attempt to create one convincing artificial person grew into an evolving social environment and a mirror for examining memory, identity, conflict, trust and the subtle behaviours that make an interaction feel human, or strangely alien.
DeJong approaches related questions through games and public participation. His projects use play to make AI ethics, media bias and information systems tangible: not to tell participants what is right or wrong, but to help them examine how they use AI, what they trust, and how individual choices connect to broader social consequences.
Moderated by Christian Beltrami, the conversation will bring these two approaches together. What happens when an AI world and a human audience confront the same questions about knowledge, fear, agency and the future? How do we know when an artificial expert deserves our trust? Can play help us think critically about AI without reducing the discussion to either enthusiasm or rejection?
Through conversation, audience prompts and game elements, the event invites participants to explore AI not as a technological spectacle, but as a tool for asking better questions about human intelligence, relationships and responsibility.

media:group.media:title: Climate Leadership Story Hub
media:group.media:description:
Montréal Climate Week Flagship Event
Join us for a screening of ᑰᒃ ᑰᑦᑐᖅ The Flowing River, a short documentary that returns to Inukjuak after the community's hydro facility is complete. Inukjuak is leading one of the largest clean-energy transitions in the Arctic.
The screening will be followed by a discussion among community partners Sarah Lisa Kasudluak, Eric Atagotaaluk, and Tommy Palliser, as well as one of Canada’s foremost energy transition commentators, Chris Henderson — all featured in the documentary — and the founder and director of the Climate Leadership Story Hub, Aphrodite Salas.
There will also be a photo gallery display of photos taken by Lina Forero during the making of the documentary.

media:group.media:title: Future Genders Archive
media:group.media:description:
What if artificial intelligence didn’t constrain, categorize, or define us, but instead opened up infinite possibilities for how we express our gender and identify?
The Future Genders Archive is a workshop series that uses speculative design and zine-making as tools of radical imagination. Join us for our program launch event to explore alternative technological worlds, learn more about the project, and create your own speculative zine artifact!
The Agenda:
Lindsay Rodgers + Jennifer Addison: Introduce Future Genders Archive workshop series + lead facilitators Casey Burkholder: Crafting as Community Building
IN PERSON ONLY Le Lin: Zine-making workshop

media:group.media:title: Grad School Myths, Busted
media:group.media:description:
Think graduate school is only for future professors? Worried it might be too expensive, too isolating, or only for students who already have everything figured out?
Join Concordia Graduate Student Ambassadors for an honest panel that tackles some of the most common myths about grad school. Students will share what they wish they had known earlier, how they made their decision, and what graduate studies actually look like once you begin. You’ll hear real perspectives on workload, funding, research and course-based programs, English-language study, finding community, and how grad school can support different academic and career goals.

media:group.media:title: Meet & Geek! - Podcast!
media:group.media:description:
Meet & Geek is a collaborative event bringing together Concordia Game Development and the Concordia Esports Students Association for a day of games, demos, and conversations around game development and gaming culture.
During the event, attendees will have the opportunity to explore and play a selection of student-made games, ranging from indie titles and VR experiences to 1v1 challenges featuring some of the most popular games. The afternoon will feature introductions and a Q&A session, giving attendees the opportunity to connect with the people behind the projects, ask questions, and learn more about game development at Concordia. We will also be presenting a special exhibition from Space Cast Magazine, so attendees can keep an eye out for some spacey art!
